title: Tower crane
prompt: A labelled scale teaching model of the pages 58 and 59 tower crane has a foundation-supported lattice tower, rotating jib assembly, counter-jib weight, trolley and hoist. Hoist winds the lifting cable through trolley and hook pulleys to raise a small payload. Trolley operates its separate cable and winch to roll along the main jib. Climb first removes the ordinary payload, extends the climbing-frame hydraulic ram to raise the top assembly, hoists the next mast section into the gap and shows it bolted in position. See-through follows the separate cable paths, winches, supporting cables, slewing gear, frame and ram. This is a scale teaching sequence, not telescopic mast growth or a complete construction procedure.
blurb: A scale teaching model traces separate trolley and hoist ropes and raises its top frame to insert a complete lattice mast section.
truthNotes: Adaptation of the 1998 and 2016 pages 56, 58 and 59. The 1988 edition is inaccessible and unverified; no edition-union claim.
Fixed foundation tower and inserted lattice section; this is not a mobile telescopic crane.
Counterweight principle is shared with the shadoof in the primary book.
Climb is a separate slowed setup with the ordinary payload grounded and detached. The rigid hydraulic frame lifts the upper assembly before a complete section is hoisted, placed, seated and bolted.
Omitted construction details include rigging labour, hydraulic supply unit, balance calculations, temporary locks, repeated strokes and final frame removal. This is not a construction procedure.
Reset replaces the teaching setup. Ropes are recoloured in see-through to distinguish their paths.
Lengths are teaching-model centimetres, not full-size crane specifications.

verification.productionTelemetry: not installed in this standalone static figure
